text:
maria: quick note — I ran a micro-experiment classifying incoming requests into prompt-size buckets + decode-rate buckets to drive continuous batching. results look promising but there are some odd KV cache interactions.

samir: nice. what buckets did you use for prompt-size?

maria: start simple: short <128 tokens, medium 128-512, long >512. decode-rate buckets: fast (>40 toks/s), normal (15-40), slow (<15).

aj: curious — how are you computing decode rate at enqueue time? we only have partial info.

maria: using first-chunk decode time window. heuristic: measure tokens_generated / time_for_first_64_toks if available, fallback to model-profiled median for that model. noisy but enough for routing.

katie: can you paste the classifier -> queue mapping?

maria: sure:
```
# pseudo-config
classifiers:
  - name: prompt_size
    buckets: [short, medium, long]
  - name: decode_rate
    buckets: [fast, normal, slow]
queue_policies:
  - name: short_fast
    max_wait_ms: 10
    token_budget_target: 192
  - name: short_normal
    max_wait_ms: 20
    token_budget_target: 256
  - name: medium_*
    max_wait_ms: 40
    token_budget_target: 384
  - name: long_*
    max_wait_ms: 80
    token_budget_target: 512
```

samir: that token_budget_target is per-batch average or per-request?

maria: per-batch average target — we scale to keep GPU occupancy while respecting latency SLO.

perf-bot: profile summary attached: avg latency short_fast=12ms, short_normal=18ms, medium=38ms, long=76ms; throughput uplift ~1.8x for short buckets.

aj: about the KV cache interactions? what did you see?

maria: for short_fast bucket we saw increased cache churn. Since batches mix many distinct prefixes, KV prefetch hit rate dropped ~12%. that increased per-token kernel selection overhead and sometimes fell back to slower matmul kernels.

katie: hmm. kernel selector needs stability — maybe prefer grouping by kv-prefix-hash when making batches, even if it slightly reduces batch size.

samir: agree. we can do a two-stage admission: first classify by prompt_size+decode_rate, then try a quick locality pass to favor same-prefix groups. fallback to filling out batch after timeout.

maria: I prototyped that: locality pass increased KV hit rate back up 9% and latency stayed within SLO, but throughput dropped ~6% for short_fast. tradeoff looks acceptable for tail p99.

aj: did you try adjusting kernel selection thresholds (attention tiling/kcache strategy) based on decode_rate bucket?

maria: yes — fast decode_rate tends to prefer smaller per-step kernels (lower launch overhead), slower decode can amortize bigger kernel launches. tweaked selection to pick low-latency kernels for fast bucket; saw 5-7% latency improvement.

katie: any perf regressions worth noting?

maria: one regression: when token_budget_target > 300 and batch mix is high, we hit a scheduling edge that increased scheduler queue wakeups — p50 stable but p99 spikes. looks like admission logic needs backpressure signals from runtime.

samir: action item: add a simple backpressure flag from runtime (queue_depth_hint) to admission, then re-run with token_budget_target sweep [128,192,256,384].

aj: I'll add the runtime metric and an endpoint so controllers can scrape it.

katie: I'll own the AB experiment config. we'll compare: baseline continuous batching vs classifier+locality+bp. metric: p99 latency, kv_hit_rate, tokens/sec, cost_per_1M_tokens.

maria: notes to add to bug/epic: 1) implement queue_depth_hint in runtime; 2) implement two-stage admission (classifier -> locality); 3) expose kernel-selection trace per-batch for debugging; 4) run full sweep and produce perf report.

perf-bot: scheduled perf job: infra/perf/17734-bucket-sweep (ETA 24h).

samir: sounds good. small nit: shorten short_fast token budget to 160 in one test — might reduce cache churn while keeping throughput.

maria: will run that variant. thanks all :thumbsup:
